newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thai official flees Hong Kong after passport scam.
newsitem.headline: Thai official flees Hong Kong after passport scam.

text.p: A Thai consular official has fled Hong Kong after being questioned by anti-corruption police in connection with soliciting bribes to issue a passport, Hong Kong government radio said on Thursday.
The unnamed suspect left the British colony after being detained and then freed by the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC), the radio said.
The man was released after his arrest on Tuesday, pending further inquiries, the ICAC said in a statement.

The anti-graft body was discussing the case with the Thai government, especially the suspect's status, it said. It is not clear if the fugitive had diplomatic status in Hong Kong, and officials from the Thai Consulate were not available for comment.

The arrest came after the ICAC received a complaint that the man had demanded a bribe of HK$100,000 (US$12,940) to issue a Thai passport, the ICAC said. At the time of his arrest, ICAC officers seized HK$100,000, it added.
The ICAC has kept a close eye on passport scams after a U.S. official was jailed for trafficking fake Honduran passports as part of an immigration racket aimed at Chinese.
